additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder (BED) is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food within a discrete time period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control over eating, and followed by marked distress. Unlike bulimia nervosa, individuals with BED do not regularly engage in inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise, and weight status can range from normal to obese. Episodes often occur in response to emotional stress, negative mood, or interpersonal difficulties, and the disorder is frequently associated with shame, secrecy, and impaired quality of life. The course can be chronic or fluctuating, with many patients presenting only after weight gain, medical concerns, or functional and emotional consequences become difficult to manage.

patient.stressor: About fourteen months ago, Janet’s mother, who had been her closest confidante in gardening, quilting, and church activities, died after a brief illness, leaving Janet with a sudden emptiness in her day-to-day routines. In the months that followed, she continued volunteering and attending farmer’s markets, but she found herself coming home to a quiet house and turning more frequently to her kitchen, baking and cooking in large batches that reminded her of family gatherings. What began as comforting herself with familiar Pennsylvania Dutch recipes gradually evolved into regularly preparing and consuming large quantities of food alone late in the evenings, especially after emotionally draining days at the food bank or when she felt guilty for forgetting appointments and letting small responsibilities slip. She sought psychiatric care after noticing her clothes no longer fit, her hiking stamina had declined, and a friend from her quilting circle gently asked if she was "using food to fill the hole" left by her mother, prompting Janet to recognize how much of her grief was playing out through her eating.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep eating big amounts of food at night even when I’m not really hungry at all.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On some nights I’ll stand at the counter and polish off half a pan of lasagna, several rolls with butter, and then go back for big bowls of ice cream, way more than anyone else in my family would’ve eaten for a whole dinner, all in the space of an hour or so before bed.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I get going, it’s like a switch flips and I’m just shoveling food in even while a little voice in my head is saying, ‘Janet, stop, you’re going to feel sick,’ but my hands just keep reaching and I don’t seem able to put the fork down.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast during these episodes that I barely chew or taste anything—just fork after fork, almost like I’m racing against something, and I only realize how quickly I’ve eaten when I look down and half the casserole dish is gone.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: Most evenings I finish a normal supper, feel comfortably full, and then around nine I wander back into the kitchen and start baking or picking at leftovers until it turns into another whole meal, even though my stomach isn’t the one asking for it—my feelings are.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: Afterward I sit there in the quiet kitchen, staring at the empty pans and wrappers, feeling heavy and ashamed and hearing my mom’s voice in my head, and I beat myself up thinking, ‘You did it again, no wonder your clothes don’t fit and you can’t hike like you used to.’

add_requirements.binge_frequency: For at least the last several months, it’s been rare for a week to go by without at least one of those nights where I end up eating huge amounts late in the evening, and some weeks it happens two or three times, especially after a hard day at the food bank or church.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve put on enough weight that I get winded on hikes I used to enjoy, my volunteer shifts feel more exhausting, and I’ve started turning down social invitations that involve food because I’m embarrassed about how I look and how I’ve been eating afterward at home.
add_requirements.duration: This pattern of late-night overeating and feeling out of control around food has been going on pretty steadily since my mom passed away about a year and a couple of months ago.
